parent.title: Decision framework: which React i18n library to adopt in 2026

siblings.title: React i18n in 2026: The Core Library Head-to-Head
siblings.summary: react-i18next is still the safe default; next-intl owns the Next.js App Router; Paraglide and Lingui are the compile-time challengers worth betting on.

siblings.title: Message format, pluralization & ICU across React i18n libraries (2026)
siblings.summary: ICU-first (react-intl, next-intl, Lingui) vs interpolation-first (i18next default, typesafe-i18n) vs MF2-inspired (Paraglide).

siblings.title: Type safety, extraction & developer tooling for React i18n in 2026
siblings.summary: Compile-first libraries (Paraglide, typesafe-i18n) and next-intl give type safety for free; i18next and react-intl bolt it on.

siblings.title: React i18n 2026: the translation pipeline, not just the library
siblings.summary: The library pins your extraction model and file format, but the TMS you pair it with decides your actual workflow.

sources.title: The most popular React localization libraries (SimpleLocalize)
sources.claim: Per-library React 19/RSC support, bundle sizes, and code-splitting for the six libraries in 2026.

sources.title: react-i18next #1616 — RSC support
sources.claim: react-i18next hooks depend on React context so Server Components need the createInstance pattern; not a native App Router fit.

sources.title: Next.js App Router i18n & Server Components (better-i18n)
sources.claim: RSC output is final HTML with no hydration step; server-resolved translations ship zero translation JS.

sources.title: next-intl — App Router getting started
sources.claim: next-intl uses awaitable getTranslations in async Server Components and useTranslations hook in Client Components; Next.js-focused.

sources.title: opral/paraglide-js
sources.claim: Paraglide is a compiler-based i18n library emitting tree-shakable translations for up to 70% smaller bundles.

sources.title: Paraglide benchmark
sources.claim: Paraglide ships 47-144 KB vs i18next 205-422 KB and stays flat as the catalog grows.

sources.title: Lingui — React Server Components tutorial
sources.claim: Lingui uses identical Trans/useLingui in server and client; server useLingui reads a per-request I18n from React cache.

sources.title: lingui/js-lingui
sources.claim: Lingui repository, ~2 kb i18n runtime, star count.

sources.title: formatjs/formatjs
sources.claim: FormatJS/react-intl repository; most complete Intl/ICU support.

sources.title: Lazy-loading i18n resources (SimpleLocalize)
sources.claim: Vite natively supports dynamic import() locale-chunk splitting; only the active locale ships initially.

sources.title: codingcommons/typesafe-i18n
sources.claim: typesafe-i18n is a lightweight (~1KB) codegen TS i18n library; last major release 2023, largely single-maintainer.

sources.title: react-i18next — SSR docs
sources.claim: react-i18next has mature, documented SSR support.

sources.title: Why I replaced i18next with Paraglide.js (dropanote)
sources.claim: Real-world migration: ~40 KB i18next reduced to ~2 KB with Paraglide.

sources.title: react-i18next vs react-intl vs Intlayer
sources.claim: react-intl is ~20KB gzipped, the heaviest option; you manage catalog splitting and lazy loading manually.

sources.title: React — Server Components reference
sources.claim: Server Components execute on the server and send only rendered output; no component JS shipped to the client.

sources.title: Next.js — Single-Page Applications guide
sources.claim: Next.js App Router can run as a strict client-side SPA where everything renders client-side.

sources.title: The Definitive Guide to i18n Libraries for Next.js & React in 2026
sources.claim: 2026 guide corroborating typesafe-i18n's smaller community and slower maintenance cadence.
